checks: The divergences sum to zero, and the flow on an oriented edge is the negative sum on its tail component. In a directed path this is Σ_{i≤j}w_i(m−m_i). The signed vertex-edge summation gives J as a tree-independent finite sum.

The closed-tail centered fiber term is nonnegative because for t below its mean it is minus the strict-lower-tail integral. The remaining term is (m_z−m) times the retained mass, with no loss at the threshold atom.

Integrating a C¹ function from a point just below the compact support and using the centered total removes the constant. Fubini gives the tail integral, and the difference of probability expectations gives the edge term. The coupling representation is the fundamental theorem of calculus on every scalar segment.

Distributionally the derivative of a closed tail of a finite signed measure is minus that measure. As a check, unit atoms at −1,+1 on two sites give edge flow 1 and J=1 on (−1,1], zero elsewhere, with derivative δ_{−1}−δ_{+1}.

For nonzero continuous normal coarea gives f_z with the factor 1/|u|, and substitution gives +(m_z−m)f_z in the within-fiber derivative and its negative in J'. The ratio is used only on positive-density intervals, so no global claim about intervening zero-density gaps is made.

The same vector edge flow projects to every cap normal; summing the individual identities keeps their actual closed tail fractions in the finite coefficients. Matched 3121a9d11f167d7d §§1–2 (1)–(8) and §7 (13)–(14).

overlap.comparison: Uses the same scalar tail correction and derivative in one explicit balanced three-fiber body. It does not give the arbitrary compact finite-measure flow formulation with threshold atoms, nor one vector flow for all cap normals.

readability: The flux is signed. The closed-tail representative is left-continuous at atoms, whereas its distributional derivative includes the full jump.
review_method: Independent cold proof read of the frozen candidate, with original-source, dependency and scope checks.
summary: The finite flow summation and fiberwise integration by parts give the closed-tail, density and joint cap identities with the stated signs, including atoms.
